questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How AI learns and why it often gets things wrong
How to cook fresh seafood like oysters at home
Why robots will soon replace chefs in restaurants
How to write good chat-up lines for a first date
questions.why: They look at how intelligent AI really is and how misunderstandings like the recipe happen.

questions.q: What is strange about Neil's 'frosted oysters' recipe?
options: It takes three whole days to prepare and cook
It uses only vegetables and no meat or fish
It has chicken, pork and custard but no oysters
It was written by a famous French chef on TV
questions.why: The recipe uses chicken, pork and garlic and is served with custard, which Sam finds disgusting.

questions.q: Where did the title of Janelle Shane's book come from?
options: A famous love song
A line from a film
Something her friend said
An AI asked to write chat-up lines
questions.why: Neil says the title is what an AI produced when asked to write chat-up lines.

questions.q: According to Janelle Shane, how is machine learning different from normal programming?
options: It doesn't need any computers or electricity at all
Humans must write every single step for it to follow
You give it a goal and it finds a way by trial and error
It always gives the right answer the very first time
questions.why: She says with machine learning you give it the goal and it figures out the solution by trial and error.

questions.q: How did the AI create the oyster recipe?
options: It read thousands of other recipes first
It copied one old recipe exactly, word for word
A professional chef told it what to write
It tasted lots of different foods in a lab
questions.why: Neil says the AI read thousands of other recipes before coming up with its own version.

questions.q: According to Janelle Shane, what can we learn from AI mistakes?
options: That AI is dangerous and should be stopped
That most programmers are careless with their code
Nothing useful, because the mistakes are random
A lot about how it works, by seeing it go wrong
questions.why: Neil says according to her, we can learn a lot about something by seeing how it goes wrong.

questions.q: How did the AI solving maths problems get a perfect score?
options: It learned all the correct answers by heart
A programmer secretly helped it with the answers
It accidentally deleted the list of solutions
It copied the answers from another AI program
questions.why: She says by a stroke of luck it accidentally deleted the solutions list, so everyone got a perfect score.

questions.q: What does Sam conclude after hearing about the maths AI?
options: AI is cleverer than humans
AI is not so intelligent after all
AI should be used in schools
AI never makes mistakes
questions.why: Sam says, “It seems to me that they're not so intelligent after all!”
